 1. **Protect capacity while you clean up.** If you're near or over quota, consider **Microsoft 365 SharePoint Storage (pay-as-you-go)** before starting cleanup work. It bills usage above the tenant quota while you reduce consumption. This solution allows you to address your cleanup effort at your own pace, and ensures you don't have to over-procure with a prepaid storage pack, since you'll only pay for what you use.  2. **Start with the biggest cleanup opportunity.**Identify what's using storage, then trim eligible versions or archive inactive content.  **Pooled-storage exception:** OneDrive storage is separate from SharePoint tenant storage unless your tenant uses a shared storage pool. In pooled-storage tenants, such as Education and trial tenants where OneDrive and SharePoint share capacity, cleaning up OneDrive can free space in that shared pool. Check your tenant's storage model before attributing savings. For Education customers, see [Pooled storage management](/en-us/microsoft-365/education/guide/1-reference/pooled-storage-management).
 
+### Recommended setup to manage storage and costs
+
+Combine usage-based capacity with version and content lifecycle policies to support growth without keeping unnecessary content in active storage.
+
+- Enable Microsoft 365 SharePoint Storage (pay-as-you-go), where eligible. Pay for usage above included capacity without prepurchasing storage packs. This provides flexibility while you clean up content and manage changing storage needs.
+- Use Automatic version history limits and trim existing versions. Microsoft recommends **Automatic** to balance recovery needs and storage efficiency without choosing version count or age limits. Apply the policy to existing libraries and trim eligible versions to match, accounting for retention and recovery requirements.
+- Use Microsoft 365 Archive for inactive content you need to keep. Archiving frees active storage quota and offers a lower storage rate for inactive content. There’s no additional Archive storage charge when combined active and archived SharePoint storage remains within licensed capacity.
+- Use content lifecycle policies to sustain the improvements. Configure inactive site and inactive files policies to archive eligible content, and retention policies to delete content after an approved period. Preview storage impact through what-if analysis or policy simulation before taking action.
+
+Together, these settings keep active storage focused on content people use, reduce unnecessary version growth, and align storage costs with usage.
+

messageCenterItems.title: Campaigns in SharePoint
messageCenterItems.summary: SharePoint is introducing site campaigns, integrating Viva Amplify's campaign management directly into SharePoint for unified creation, distribution, and analytics of news posts. Available to both seeded and licensed Viva Amplify users, rollout begins mid-August 2026. No changes to existing Amplify campaigns or licensing.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and Why:

Today we're sharing an update to the new/upcoming SharePoint Publish experience: campaigns in SharePoint (site campaigns). This new capability brings Viva Amplify's campaign management natively into SharePoint, giving corporate communications teams a unified place to create, distribute, and measure their news without leaving the platform where their news content already lives.

This feature applies to both seeded SharePoint users and premium users licensed for Viva Amplify. Amplify users can continue to create Amplify app campaigns as they see fit. This new feature provides a complementary way to create lighter weight campaigns inside a SharePoint site as a way to organize your SharePoint news posts and benefit from campaign analytics directly from SharePoint. There are no changes to Viva Amplify's license model. Note: Amplify 'create campaign' settings in the admin center only apply to Amplify app campaigns.

Rollout Schedule:

Preview (if applicable): Not Applicable

Targeted Release (if applicable): Late July to August 2026

Standard Release (if applicable): August - Sept 2026

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on mid August 2026 and expect to complete by end of November 2026.

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected:

• SharePoint and Viva Amplify users and corporate communications teams that publish and manage SharePoint news.

Platforms/Services:

• SharePoint Online, Viva Amplify.

What will happen:

  • Amplify users can continue to create and manage campaigns in the Viva Amplify app.
  • A new SharePoint experience will allow users to create lightweight site campaigns directly within SharePoint.
  • Site campaigns can be used to organize related SharePoint news posts, and publish these news posts across SharePoint, Viva Engage, Teams and Outlook Email.
  • Users will have access to campaign analytics from within SharePoint.
  • There are no changes to the existing Viva Amplify campaign experience.
  • The feature is available to both seeded SharePoint users and premium users licensed for Viva Amplify.

Action Required/Recommendations:

There is no action for admins beyond reviewing any internal help or guidance you may have created for end users.

  • Review internal documentation and prepare end-user guidance as appropriate.
  • Communicate the availability of SharePoint site campaigns to appropriate SharePoint users, Viva Amplify users, corporate communications and content publishing teams.
  • Be aware that the Viva Amplify Create campaign admin setting applies only to campaigns created in the Viva Amplify app and does not govern SharePoint site campaigns.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.
